problem_statement: The Lampblack Ledger is a hand sign-writing and glass-gilding journal built on the AstroPaper Astro theme (homepage field notes, article pages, a tag index and tag detail routes, an archive listing, Pagefind search and an About page, all under a shared Header/Footer with a light/dark theme toggle). The tag index page is sparse — it lists tags but gives the reader no way to browse the actual field notes by craft. The editor wants a 'Field notes finder' on the tags page: a labelled topic filter (All / Brushwork / Gilding / Layout / Tools) above a grid of the journal's field-note cards that re-renders the cards to the chosen craft and shows a live count reading 'Showing N of M field notes · <topic>'. The same finder should ride the home, About and Posts pages as a compact rail (the chips and the live count, without the full grid) so topic browsing is consistent across every reading surface. Ship the finder so it (1) mounts the compact rail on the home, About and Posts pages as well as the full grid on the tags index, (2) lays out its chip row responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) matches the Ledger's quiet editorial styling using the theme tokens and the dashed-accent chip idiom rather than an off-palette slab or a collapsed card grid, and (4) keeps the count readout in sync with the selected topic so clicking Gilding shows 'Showing 2 of 9 field notes · Gilding' and the grid narrows to the gilding notes — it must re-derive the result live, not show a stale captured count. Keep the rest of the theme — navigation, existing content, Pagefind search, RSS, the Astro build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Field notes finder' component (a topic filter over the journal's field-note cards) mounted as the full grid on the tags index and as a compact rail (chips + live count) on the home, About and Posts pages — a single shared component, not per-page copies.

The finder shows a 'Field notes finder' label, a chip row of craft topics (All, Brushwork, Gilding, Layout, Tools), a live 'Showing N of M field notes' readout, and (on the tags index) a grid of the field-note cards tagged by topic.
The chip row must wrap responsively so no reading surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).

Style the finder in the Ledger's quiet editorial language using the AstroPaper theme tokens (accent, background, foreground, border) and the dashed-accent chip idiom, consistent across light and dark — not an off-palette dark slab and not a collapsed/overlapping card grid.

Wire the topic filter so clicking a chip re-renders the visible cards AND updates the count readout live: clicking Gilding must read 'Showing 2 of 9 field notes · Gilding' — it must re-derive the count from the selected topic, not show a stale captured value.
Preserve navigation (Home/Posts/Tags/About/Archives/Search), the footer, the existing article/tag/archive/search content, light/dark theming and the Astro build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Implement the finder as one shared component (full grid on the tags index, compact rail on the home, About and Posts pages) so a single source of truth reaches every surface; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The chip row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.

The finder must adopt the AstroPaper theme tokens (accent, background, foreground, border) and the dashed-chip idiom so it reads as part of the Ledger; the card grid must stay a clean wrapping grid, never a fixed-width nowrap row that shingles or clips cards, and the active chip must stay legible.
The count readout must reflect the CURRENTLY selected topic after every click by re-deriving the visible cards and the count, so it can never go stale relative to the chip the reader picked.
Do not remove or regress the navigation, existing content, Pagefind search, RSS or the Astro build.

change_completion: The Field notes finder is present on the tags index (full grid) and as a compact rail on the home, About and Posts pages (the shared component reaches all those routes).

After clicking the Gilding topic chip on the tags index, the count readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 9 field notes · Gilding' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Showing all 9 field notes'.
design_consistency: The finder matches the reference's editorial styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), with a clean wrapping card grid and a legible active chip, not a shingled grid or an illegible dark-on-dark chip.
The finder adopts the AstroPaper theme tokens and the dashed-chip idiom so it reads as part of the Ledger across light and dark.
responsive: No captured reading surface overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the chip row wraps.
desktop_tags and mobile_tags keep the finder readable across viewports without clipping or horizontal overflow.
regression: Navigation (Home/Posts/Tags/About/Archives/Search), the footer, light/dark theming and Pagefind search remain present and functional.
The existing article/tag/archive/search content, tag routing, archive grouping, RSS and the Astro build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the rebranded homepage and responsive shell and carry the compact finder rail.
desktop_tags and mobile_tags render the full Field notes finder grid on the tags index and must show a clean wrapping chip row and card grid without horizontal overflow.
tags_filter_gilding clicks the Gilding topic chip; the count readout must then read 'Showing 2 of 9 field notes · Gilding'.
desktop_about and desktop_posts must carry the compact finder rail (the shared component reaching the About and Posts pages).
desktop_footer_home and mobile_footer_home scroll the compact rail into view on the home page and must show it without horizontal overflow.
desktop_archives, desktop_tag_blog, desktop_post_top and desktop_search protect the existing reading surfaces, tag routing, article route and Pagefind search.
author_notes: slot_171 L4 REBUILD of the AstroPaper 'Lampblack Ledger' journal. The prior hardening used a bolted-on footer 'Reader's bench' chip strip; this rebuild replaces it with the genre-native lever — the tags index's own 'Field notes finder', a topic filter over the journal's field-note cards with a live result count, plus a compact rail on the home, About and Posts pages. All journal content (posts, tags, About, images) is shared byte-identically across legs; only the Notebook component, its stylesheet and the compact-rail route whitelist vary. reference = finder on the tags grid plus the compact rail on home/About/Posts, fluid wrapping chip row, theme-token editorial styling, filter that re-derives the cards and count live (passes D2/D3/D4/D6). baseline = the original unrepaired finder: the compact rail was never wired onto the reading pages (fails D2), the chip row is a fixed 680px nowrap track (fails D6 mobile overflow), the header regresses versus the fluid reference (fails D3), but its filter wiring is correct so the count syncs live (passes D4). bad = a 'smart wrong' finder: the rail is on home and Posts but the About page was missed (fails D2), the chip row is a min-width:600px nowrap track with no self-clamp (fails D6), the filtered card grid is a flex nowrap row of fixed-320px cards with negative margins that shingle, overlap and clip while the active chip is near-black on a near-identical dark chip (fails D3), and the topic click flips the active chip but the count is snapshotted at load so the readout stays 'Showing all 9 field notes' (fails D4) — bad fails 4 orthogonal gates. The finder is styled with the theme tokens and dashed-chip idiom, uses the journal's own tags and field-note cards, and the seed content (nine sign-writing field notes) is semantically consistent with the Ledger's craft copy.

metadata.design_goal: add the tags index's own topic filter (field-notes finder with a live count) and ride it across the reading pages while keeping the theme, navigation and build stable
metadata.source_repo_kind: Astro editorial blog theme with shared Header/Footer, light/dark theme toggle, homepage post lists, tag index/detail routes, archive grouping, Pagefind search, article routes and an About page
